newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil chief blasts carbon dioxide tax proposal.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil chief blasts carbon dioxide tax proposal.

text.p: Japan's oil industry chief has strongly criticised the possible introduction of a carbon dioxide tax on fossil fuels now being discussed by the government, an industry spokesman said on Wednesday.
Yuji Idemitsu, Petroleum Association of Japan (PAJ) chairman, was quoted by a PAJ spokesman as saying : "(The tax) targets specific industrial sectors."

A tax on carbon dioxide emissions is an attempt by the government to secure an easy way to increase tax revenues, Idemitsu, who is also president of leading refiner Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd, was quoted as saying.
Idemitsu also said that oil products were a necessity, and that imposing a higher level of tax on them was unlikely to cut the consumption of fossil fuels drastically.

Idemitsu's comments, made at a news conference in Hokkaido in northern Japan on Tuesday, were triggered by a recent report released by a study group affiliated with the government's Environment Agency.
The report, released on Friday, offered some suggestions on how a carbon dioxide tax might be introduced.
This included a proposal to impose a tax on products which emit carbon dioxide, with the level of taxation depending on the size of emissions.
